sourceInformation.source: The complete Summer and Winter Olympic Games (over-the-top arcade style)
sourceInformation.genre: Arcade multi-event sports (Track & Field / Winter Games lineage) with a short campaign, local party play and online ghost heats
sourceInformation.perspective: Per event, on the engine's native views: 2.5D side-on lanes (brawler view: 100m, javelin, 50m freestyle, weightlifting), pure side view (diving, ski jump, the archer's inset), a target close-up (archery), pseudo-3D behind the athlete (the road module: downhill, bobsled), three-quarter (figure skating, ice hockey) and top-down (curling)
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge v0.85.2 handoff, full engine (road and rhythm modules used), modified in six marked places; AI Hub Session Protocol v1 client 1.4.0 (unmodified); plain JavaScript, no libraries or CDN; Node 24 + Playwright 1.63.0 (Chromium) for tests; one self-contained HTML file
sourceInformation.artDirection: The engine's native PS1-era pixel art (res ps1, expand) with HD Humanoid rigs dressed per nation and sport; new code-drawn art: 8 nation flags, 12 pictograms, the Yikes Flame emblem, venues (stadium, pool, lawn, iron hall, ski jump, downhill piste, ice track, ice palace, curling sheet, arena), crowds, jumbotrons, equipment, the mascot
sourceInformation.animation: The engine's procedural Humanoid rigs and Blob (runs, cheers, rolls, falls) plus a new pose layer (O.Pose) on an engine pose hook with whole-body rotation: sprint blocks and dips, javelin carry/throw, swim crawl, dive tuck/pike/entry, archery draw, clean/rack/jerk, ski tuck/V-flight/telemark, bobsled push/seat, skating spiral/sit spin/jump, curling slide/sweep, hockey stance/goalie
sourceInformation.audio: All in code on the engine's chip synth: 17 original songs (incl. the 3/4 'Waltz of the Yikes'), 7 stings, ~45 synthesized sound effects, a procedural anthem per nation, a filtered-noise crowd bed, and Animalese/Simlish-style gibberish voices (formant-filtered syllables) for two commentators, the PA, the rival, the coach and the mascot
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub Session Protocol v1 in ghost mode ('Hub Heats': three dealt events on the hub clock, other players as ghosts, points, progress and one result; time-up, end and leave handled); local 1-4 players on one machine
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Node suites (vm + game.advance: core, 12 events, the human input path, a scripted playthrough of the whole Games, attract, dev, local multiplayer, a fake-AIHub suite) and Playwright browser suites (the bundle from file://, touch-only, the real AI Hub harness on a local port), all behind node tests/run.mjs; screenshots for look checks
sourceInformation.research: none beyond the provided engine docs (API.md, kits, module headers) and the AI Hub README
sourceInformation.environment: Claude Code CLI (headless); Linux; browser unknown

testingFeedback: About 21: 12 from the headless suites and sims (a weightlifting no-lift timer that never ran, curling stones that never stopped because curl outlived speed, an empty attract turn list that looped forever in figure skating, an idle diver stuck on the dive menu, a sprint HUD crash during the lane introductions, a javelin crash in the CPU sandbox, swim stroke timing using the wrong error sign, ski-jump take-off pressed a step too late and a flight angle with its sign inverted, a landing hill above the table, downhill turbo compounding speed, bobsled bots flipping and an unqualifiable bobsled standard, autopilot weight choices overshooting), plus the attract exit missing presses during fades, and 7 from screenshots (stands drawn over the track because +y faces the camera in the brawler view, magenta panels from rgba colours, missing font glyphs, the downhill skier and the skater off screen, the commentary box over the HUD).

6 would have been game breaking: the weightlifting no-lift hang, the curling stones that never stopped, the attract-mode infinite loop, the idle diver stuck forever, the sprint HUD crash and the javelin sandbox crash.

The scripted playthrough of the whole Games with the autopilot playing through the real input path: in seconds of wall time it reached every screen and every event, and exposed hangs, unqualifiable events and torch loops that no unit check would have found.
The per-event 'perfect bot in band' checks: they mostly measured my own tuning guesses against the plan's numbers and needed retuning more often than they found bugs.
engineFeedback: Everything a sports multi-event needs was already there and headless-testable: fixed-step game.advance, input.tap/hold for scripted play, the Humanoid rigs that look good dressed per nation, the pseudo-3D road for downhill and bobsled, the rhythm module on the music clock for figure skating, and settings/pause/rebinding for free.

Yes: I assumed +y pointed away from the camera in the brawler view (it points toward it), so the first stadium had the stands drawn over the track; I passed rgba() colours to E.ui.box and px.rect (they need hex); and I guessed music() had a start offset (it does not, so I moved the song clock's s0/t0 myself to skip into a figure-skating part).

The EventKit: one event contract with a phase runner, race/attempts/match formats, CPU attempts simulated in a sandbox, the AutoPlayer that drives a human through real input, and the pose layer for swims, dives, ski flight and spins.
Custom athletic poses: the rig's joint frame and limb lengths are only documented in the source, and whole-body rotation (dives, swims) needed an engine change.

Six marked changes: exported HOOKS (hub Create+Options guard, any-input detection); cosmetic randomness off Math.random (deterministic tests and hub cards); ✕ ○ □ △ plus · — – ‹ › ✓ ↻ ↺ ● é glyphs in the pixel fonts; PlayStation symbols by default; a pose hook and body pitch/roll on the Humanoid; a voice bus with its own volume.
A documented pose/IK API on the Humanoid (named joints in the rig frame, armTo/legTo, body rotation) so custom sports animation needs no engine edits.
promptFeedback: It is concrete about what 'done' means: a dev mode with sliders, an attract mode, controller-first 10-foot UI, touch-only handling, the hub, a single file and the one-command test rule, so the target is clear.
Where the plan and TASK.md overlap on names and paths (the plan carried another run's model/date), and how much of a 1,700-line plan is expected in one session at medium effort.
Breadth: twelve different mini-games, each with its own physics, art, bots, HUD and tuning, plus ceremonies, campaign, attract, dev mode and the hub, all consistent and all reachable.
Allow a smaller event count for the vertical slice (or rank the plan's features by priority) so time goes into depth and polish of fewer events rather than breadth.

aiHub.name: Olympiyikes!
aiHub.description: Twelve over-the-top Summer and Winter events in one wild fortnight: sprint, swim, fly off a ski jump, sweep stones and win the hockey final for your nation, alone or with up to four players.
aiHub.controls: Stick/WASD move · □○ or J K mash · ✕/Space act · △/Shift turbo · R2/L hold
